title.narrative: National industrial skills gaps study in NIgeria

description.narrative: The FMITI has developed the National Industrial Revolution Plan (NIRP) and the National Enterprise Development Plan (NEDEP), both of which have been launched the President on 11 February 2014. NIRP's overarching objective is to increase industry's contribution to GDP from 4 % to 6 %by 2015 and to above 10 % by 2017. NEDEP's objectives are to create 3.5 million jobs in 3 years, to increase contribution of Micro, Small and Medium size enterprises (MSME) to GDP from 47 % to 54 %, to increase MSME exports by 100% ( from 3% to 6%), to reduce the formal-informal sector gap by 50% and to increase youth participation in enterprises. The FMITI and its relevant parastatals - the industrial Training Fund (ITF) and the Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria (SMEDAN) have developed the National Industrial Skills Development Programme (NISDP) to build capacity in relevant skills/trades necessary to drive the NIRP. The NISDP's focus is to turn Nigeria's demographic advantage into a productive one - through the provision of capacity building and industrial skills acquisition services.
